newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Jan 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Jan 20.

text.p: Leading food service operator Kyotaru Co Ltd, listed on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange, filed for protection from creditors with Tokyo District Court on Sunday, citing 101.3 billion yen in debt on a consolidated basis from investment losses and poor performance of its mainline take-out sushi business.

Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp will offer subscribers signing up for its Integrated Services Digital Circuits (ISDN) service the option of paying slightly higher monthly basic fees and no initial fee, starting in July. New ISDN subscribers are expected to reach 800,000 for the year to March.

The "Big Four" securities houses, including Nomura Securities Co Ltd and Nikko Securities Co Ltd, are resorting to subordinated debt to proceed with their plans to unload non-performing assets at affiliated non-banks. The move reflects the plunge in share prices on the Tokyo stock market since early this month.

Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd plans to start selling DVD (digital video disc) players overseas this month in seven Asian countries including Thailand and Singapore. It also will sell DVD players in the United States from March 1. Matsushita hopes to gain more than 30 percent of a world market which is estimated at two million DVD players in 1997. The five other Asian countries are Indonesia, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Malaysia and the Philippines.
